Why doesn't recirculate work when defrost is on? (tl;dr in comments)

tl;dr: Basically the air inside the car has more moisture due to breath and perspiration, which would fog up the windshield worse.

I just found this as the top result from searching what I titled the post. It's something I've wondered for years and hadn't bothered to look up until now.

Some of the commenters in that thread mention that AC + heat + defrost is the best combo, because of the AC compressor kicking on. Why is that? Nobody explained the AC compressor part.
Cooling the air with the AC dries it. It is then heated and blown onto the windshield.
Cold air has less ability to hold moisture. As the air cold the water vapor condenses into water that drains away. When the air is reheated it maintains it's new lower humidity.
Not all cars are like that. My current primary ride will let you go 'old school' with the heat and a/c at the same time on defrost. Works like a champ. The a/c takes the moisture out of the air.
Why does the AC take the moisture out of the air? Can your car recirculate with defrost on?

It's the same principle as what makes it rain: when air cools it shrinks (shrinkage!) and becomes more sense. It is no longer able to hold moisture. The a/c system is designed to deal with the water - that's where the water puddle under your car comes from when you have the a/c on. Same with the a/c at your house.
Thanks for the explanation. What's your main ride? I've only owned a handful of vehicles, but none of them would allow defrost with recirc.

I have a sports car that won't allow recirculation and defrost. I gave a car to my nephew and that one would open vents and all that on its own. It wouldn't even allow the a/c to be on under a certain temperature - it insisted that the outside vents be open. My company provided vehicle also allows recirculation and heat / defrost / a/c at the same time. So it varies from vehicle to vehicle.
Defrost has the job of removing moisture from the passenger compartment. If the air is recirculating The moisture is recirculating as well.
